name: AIRWA setBurnRate() has no owner check
summary: AIRWA.setBurnRate(uint256) lacked an owner check and the burn on transfers to the pair takes that rate of the pair's own balance. The attacker set the rate to 98%, sent a zero-value transfer to the pair to burn its AIRWA, reset the rate and sold into the inflated price for the pair's USDT.
notes: Reset: the first sale into the pair (0xdd7e30d3 by 0xc43b939b, block 48038614, 303 blocks after deployment) recorded the trading start time in slot 0x11, written only this once. The runtime is unverified, but replays of the anchor revert "sell" with that slot cleared or less than two hours old and succeed once it is two hours old, so this launch start time first made the exploit's sales possible (rule 8); the two hours passed eight hours before the anchor. The owner's own setBurnRate(0) (0x4d4081ac) is not a reset. Loss is the AIRWA/USDT pair's USDT; its burned AIRWA is valued at nothing (rule 12).
